title: continue: Skipping the Current Iteration
learningObjectives: Explain continue: skipping the current iteration and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: continue skips the remaining body statements for this pass and moves to the next iteration. A for loop still performs its update; a while loop rechecks its condition.
understand.whyItMatters: Filtering logic can be clearer when unwanted values are skipped early.
understand.explain: Ensure state changes happen before continue when needed, especially in while loops.

examples.title: Skip odd values
examples.explanation: The for update still occurs after continue.

examples.title: Skip zero
examples.explanation: Zero is ignored; remaining elements are processed.

examples.title: while safely advances
examples.explanation: Increment occurs before continue, avoiding a stuck loop.

examples.title: Filter passing scores
examples.explanation: Only scores at least 50 are printed.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five continue: Skipping the Current Iteration examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating continue: skipping the current iteration in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Place continue after required state updates.
For loops still perform their update.
while loops go back to condition.
Ensure skipped cases do not stall state.
